newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end mixed, Sept S&P up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end mixed, Sept S&P up.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended mixed, with Standard & Poor's 500 (S&P 500) futures recovering with Treasury bonds.

September S&Ps ended firm, tracking a late rebound in Treasuries that was triggered by reported comments from Federal Reserve Governor Susan Phillips. Traders took Phillips comments -- reported in a wire service interview -- to mean interest rates may not need to be raised over the near term.
September S&P 500s edged to a new session high at 944.00 in afternoon trade, but remained within Friday's overall 926.75 to 956.00 range.
"We came back a little today," an S&P 500 futures trader said. "Sanity was restored."
On Friday, stock index futures posted steep losses as U.S. assets crumbled heading into the weekend.
"Bonds kind of helped and we saw some short-covering off of the low," the S&P 500 trader said.
Traders said the afternoon rally saw strong volume initially, but said interest tapered off into the close.
"It was pretty uneventful towards the end of the day," another S&P 500 futures trader said.
Traders await upcoming key U.S. data.
Several traders said the risk was that Wednesday's July retail sales would show a pick-up in the economy's pace.
A Reuter poll of economists showed an average forecast for up 0.7 percent overall and up 0.5 percent excluding autos.
Also Wednesday is July producer prices, with consumer prices due on Thursday.
Nikkei 225 futures ended down after continuing an overnight slide. September Nikkei closed below 19,000 and at the lowest price since late April.

At the close, September S&P 500s were up 6.15 points at 942.55, KCBT Value Lines were 3.75 higher at 839.25, new composites were 2.75 higher at 487.80, Midcap 400s were 0.40 higher at 313.15, Russell 2000s were down 0.95 at 413.55, and Nikkeis were 215 lower at 18,960.
